question: Which Five-Year Plan introduced the concept of 'family planning' as a significant objective?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74)** formally emphasized **family planning as a major national objective** to control population growth.
 
• It strengthened the existing programme by promoting **modern contraceptive methods** and expanding family welfare services.
 
• The plan linked population stabilisation with **economic development and poverty reduction**, recognising its significance for national growth.
 
• Major thrust was given to **institution-based programs, community health workers**, and improved distribution of contraceptives.
 
• The plan also aimed to create **awareness campaigns** to encourage responsible family planning practices across rural and urban India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)**

 
 
• India became the first nation to launch an official **family planning programme in 1952**.
 
• Focus on **maternal and child health** services and awareness-based FP approach.
 
• Laid foundation for population control measures post-Independence.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)**
 
 
• Strengthened family planning clinics and distribution of **birth control measures**.
 
• Introduced **target-based approach** for early family planning initiatives.
 
 
 
• **National Population Policy (2000)**
 
 
• Aimed to achieve **stable population by 2045**.
 
• Focus on **reproductive health, education, and girl-child empowerment**.
 
• Stressed voluntary and informed choice in **family planning services**.
